# Module 10: Finance, timesheets and admin

*Bills checked, debtors chased and payroll right, without the Friday scramble.*

**Who does it in a small business:** Owner, bookkeeper, office admin.

## The typical process

Every business does it a bit differently. This is the common shape we see.

| # | Step | What happens | Tools | Where time goes |
|:-:|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Bills come in | Match to the order and delivery docket | Xero, MYOB, PDF | slow |
| 2 | Approve and pay | Approved, paid, filed (often three places) | Xero, Bank portal, SharePoint | copy-paste |
| 3 | Timesheets | Hours in, checked, approved | Field app, Excel | slow |
| 4 | Payroll | Checked employee by employee | Xero, Employment Hero | slow |
| 5 | Invoice and chase | Invoices out, debtors chased by phone | Xero, Phone | slow |
| 6 | Weekly numbers | The report pulled together by hand | Excel | copy-paste |

## Where the time goes

From businesses APG has audited, anonymised. Hours are staff estimates, not measurements.

- Each bill saved in three places: about 4 h a week
- Chasing debtors: about 12 h a week for one bookkeeper
- New starters set up in three systems: about 2 h each
- Receipts only on one phone, so the books stop when it's away

## Step 1: the intake

"How we do it" (planned): Map your office week: bills, timesheets, payroll, invoicing, chasing, and who does each.

It hands back your own version of the map above, with your tools and your hours, then suggests which skill to build first.

## The skills

- **Bill checker** (connected): Bill against order and docket; only the mismatches come to you
- **Debtor chase list** (connected): Who to chase today, emails drafted
- **Payroll check** (connected): Hours against pay, exceptions only. Being built
